title: Simultaneous Sine99 pitch-ratio audit
status: Measurement-only; frozen primary and separately frozen posthoc extension complete. No production adoption.
scope: All original19 v5 Sine99 windows, fixed half subdivisions of the two original primary simultaneous67/75 pairs, existing Opus/AAC/native media, analytic stationary controls. Reused upload is not an independent hardware holdout.
conclusion: A roughly−0.48-cent compression of the captured simultaneous67/75 interval survives both encodes, four control-qualified estimators and all fixed mid subdivisions. Uniform common captured mistuning cannot alone explain that ratio. Single-channel/window sensitivity and shared-master/capture/output-effect confounds remain. No YM3420 clock, FNUM law, arithmetic width or per-note correction is identified.

interpretation_limits: Sameupload AAC/Opus are not independent hardware captures or a source master.
Common tuning, uniform timebase or resampling shifts both captured cents but cancels from simultaneous intervalerror. Frequency-dependent dynamics, Chorus and priornotes canbias estimates.
Pitch-grid evidence cannot determine OPUclock, arithmetic widths, FNUMtable or DACupdate rate.
Legacy full/half window observations are correlated; no independent-error confidence intervals or pernote tuning adopted.

protocol.status: Frozen after primary result, before exploratory endpoint extraction. This is explicitly posthoc and does not alter primary acceptance.
protocol.method: For each source/channel/note, use the original whole-window Hann spectral frequency from the frozen result only as demodulation center. Fixed 4th-order zero-phase Butterworth, .5 s context around fixed endpoints, retain full 48 kHz unwrapped complex phase. Interpolate unwrapped phase linearly at the exact declared start/end, add spectral center and divide phase change by 2*pi*duration. No OLS or new frequency/time fit. Report endpoint amplitudes relative to median and minimum amplitude across interval, do not reject observations.
protocol.interpretation: A fixed full period can cancel strictly periodic phase if the declared RecordedChorus period describes the actual capture and no phase-zero/pathology prevents endpoint comparison. The actual analog wet contribution need not cancel in mid or have this period; amplitude changes, phase crossings, Reverb and capture processing remain.
